Sextortion

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Often it's young vulnerable girls that are taken advantage of in the online space, but Sextortion, an online catfishing crime is on the rise in South Africa and the victims are of all ages and sexes.

Unique Selling Point:
It’s the new form of sexual harassment. Sextortion refers to a form of blackmail in which sexual information or images are used to extort sexual favors and money from the victim. Social media and text messages are often the source of the sexual material and the threatened means, used to share it with others.

Summary:
In South Africa incidents of Sextortion have been on the rise from 2016 and to date, more and more individuals are falling for it. It used to be that the primary targets and victims for such online attacks are young vulnerable females, but this has since escalated to older victims being blackmailed for cash. With online dating sites such as Tinder, Zoosk and Grinder more adults are targets of the scams. Unscrupulous individuals are lurking on the Internet ready to pounce on unsuspecting victims.

Your computer webcam, cellphone and online chats can be hacked by an unknown stranger who will be able to access all intimate information about you. The unknown individual will then invite you to a social media platform, be it Watsapp, Facebook, etc. They would then proceed to blackmail you for money or to perform sexually explicit activities such as sending nude pictures, videos or such. They will then threaten you with publicizing your intimate information on the Internet or alerting your loved ones, church congregations and colleagues of all the information they have.


Further information:
Mike Bolhuis a private investigator has recently had quite a few clients who have approached him to catch the perpetrators or catfish, as they are extorting his clients for a lot of money, to such an extent that they say to their victim, if you don't deposit the money within the next 20 minutes we will publish your information. They then harass the person to take pictures of themselves whilst they are depositing the money and to tell them what they are doing every step of the way. They are also embarrassed and feel they have no recourse, which is why they are approaching a private investigator.

According to Dudu Nhlabathi, a Psychologist, traditionally females have been victims that fall for this scam, but now males are equally vulnerable. Males tend to be under the illusion that women are not capable of doing such things, and they feel physically superior, so they tend not to feel the danger. The scamsters study psychological methods when identifying their targets as well. With women It is normally low self-esteem individuals who would be identified for instance those who never post full body pictures on the social media platforms are easily spotted. When it comes to male victims, if they are flashy they can be a target, or if they hold jobs that would be compromised if they are exposed, especially if they are family men they will become instantly vulnerable to sextortion. The scammers appear to be their friends at first to earn their trust and then they pounce once the victims fall for them, or they purely engage with the male victims for a bit of online sexual fun and games. Dr Nhlabathi deals both with Victims and perpetrators. Carte Blanche will possibly also speak to one of the scammers.

It is quite clear that the online space is increasingly and quickly becoming a space where people are vulnerable to being blackmailed for their private vices or supposed fun. The search for reassurance and belonging is driving unsuspecting victims to a world of horror and pain. Is there a way to stop these perpetrators and can the victims get retribution? Carte Blanche investigates.

Press Release:

It’s a form of blackmail in which sexual information or images willingly shared by the victim are used to extort money from them. Across South Africa, the numbers of incidents of sextortion have increased exponentially. Carte Blanche investigates.

Script:


Jonathan: I was on the Internet browsing and a popup appeared, saying meet singles in your area

VO: Jonathan was in a steady relationship at the time and his story is one of many that start with an innocent “Hi”

Jonathan: and i clicked on it and there’s a cell phone number, and I took the cellphone number and I sent a whatsapp.

VO: Dudu Nhlabathi a dating and life coach, says it’s not unusual for people to meet online.

Dudu: The internet has given birth to a hook up culture and it has normalized that. so when you're getting a random hello, when you’re getting a random inbox and you've been on the likes of other dating sites if you're used to that, getting a hi. Its less alarming than 20 years ago.

LINK:
Have you ever shared intimate details about yourself online with a stranger? If you have, your biggest fear may be, are you being catfished? Is the person on the other side who they say they are?// Many South African men are falling prey to a menacing strain of catfishing on social media platforms.

VO: Eighteen year old Jason was duped this way.

Jason: I was just browsing on facebook as i usually do and i got a friend request which i accepted and almost immediately i got a message saying hi contact me on whatsapp


VO: All the men we spoke to wish to remain anonymous for fear of shame and recrimination. Pedro who is a married man with two children, was also browsing on facebook when he received his friend request whilst still at work.

Pedro: I was going to her profile and I see we have mutual friends as I saw that I thought, oh well, it’s probably somebody from school or university and I accepted the request.

VO: In each of these cases, the girl on the other side sent naked pictures of herself in sexually explicit poses and enticed the man to do the same.

Jonathan: I didn’t reply at once and then she sent more pictures. Then she said oh well just send me a picture of your face and i thought, ok well, that cant do any harm.

Devi: so what picture did you send her?

Jason: just of myself down there and then she asked no can i have one of your sexy body and that is when i sent one of my face

Devi: She wanted a picture of your face, so you sent like a ID pic, smiling, and then what did she say?

Jonathan: She likes what she’s seeing and then she sends more naked pictures and then she said well just send a picture of yourself, naked, and i made the biggest mistake of my life and i did

Pedro: The picture that she sent me was very erotic. To a point were she also sent a video, that was very, very, erotic. Returning a favour I then went and took a picture of myself.

VO: It doesn’t take long after the victims have sent their full body naked pictures for the sextortion to start and it’s relentless.

Jason: she sent me a screenshot of all of my contacts with that image and the send button saying that if i don’t send one thousand five hundred rand immediately she will share those images. My whole body went white, i literally felt like fainting.

Jonathan: we've got your number, we’ve got your pictures, now we need first it was three hundred rand then it was five hundred rand

Devi: what were they threatening you with

Jonathan: just to post everything all over

VO: Jonathan knew immediately he’d been scammed, but Pedro was a bit more naive and still believed the girl was a university student.

Pedro: She sent a message that said my mother just died, can you please send me money

VO: But when he refused her, the threats came fast and furious.

Pedro: When I declined she sent me photos of myself and my family and the photos that I just sent her altogether in a nice collage, and threatening me that if I don’t pay her two thousand rand now, she’s going to put this on Facebook.

VO: Specialist Investigator Mike Bolhuis has taken on these cases of sextortion.

Mike: this has been going on for quite some time. We need to take note that internet crime, knocks and scams is an ongoing crime and is escalating. Its probably the biggest crimes in the world presently.

Devi: when did you hear about the first case

Mike: it was about march. The guy called me hes very embarrassed but he has no other option but to ask my advice. We're up to 40 now and we're getting more

VO: Pedro and Jonathan started paying up, but Jason was young and didn’t have that sort of money, so he had to tell someone and he turned to his dad.
Jason: I just looked at him and said this is the end of my life. Jobs check your facebook, How am i going to get a job one day, how am i going to carry on with school. He said calm down we'll take it step by step.

Jason: it was a big shock in the back of my mind i knew i might not be talking to this girl but still you are a teenager and you thinking with your hormones and not with your brain.

Mike: Their main aim is to get money. They don't know what you have and if you're a rich man or not. They do a test and its R1000 but it escalates. The biggest case i have is about R50000.

VO: When Mike gets involved he gives the victims specific instructions to follow.

Jason: That’s when Mike Bolhuis told my dad to tell them listen here, we stay on a farm
My dad took my phone and spoke on my behalf and started catfishing them and trying to buy time.


VO: If the victim tries to buy time, the price goes up, and even if the victim pays - the price goes up. The intimidation is constant.



Mike: They would give account numbers at supermarkets where you would pay it in. They have no problem saying to you drive here and drive there.

VO: They use scare tactics like fake headlines and bogus shots of policemen who are supposedly now onto the victim.

Jonathan: You get scared. Surely it can’t be posted on the front of a newspaper but when you see it you think shit maybe it can.

LINK : So what kind of person is most likely to fall prey to a catfish scam and how do these criminal gangs target their victims?

VO: Dr Ian Opperman is an educational and clinical psychologist.
Ian: Males by nature are hunters in relationships so there’s a huge emphasis on sex and sexuality.
The average guy feels stuck in his marriage, not getting attention, his sex life is not as good as it should be and the next thing he thinand he sends a picture of himself this is a nice opportunity….
Dudu: You’re meeting a beautiful girl on social media shes more than likely to share some sexy pictures with you. Shes willing to do what most women wouldn't do, what your wife wont do, things you've never heard of.
They look for someone whose got something to lose. You can’t blackmail someone who doesn’t have anything to lose.
Pedro: It made me feel like my family is in danger now and I would do anything to protect my family. They know where I was staying, they knew where I was working, it won’t take long for them to come and put a knife against my throat at work, it won’t take long to ambush my wife in front of my estate.
Ian: If you get caught the shame becomes public, there’s money involved, you might have to tell your wife and children who think their father is some big man in society has to admit that he hasn’t been as pure as what he pretended to be.

VO: Jonathan felt he had to tell his girlfriend, but their relationship is now on rocky ground.

Jonathan: It changed a lot. from a relationship point of view to get the trust back i don’t know how you’re going to do it.

VO: In the cases that Mike Bolhuis has investigated, he says the con men are operating out of Hillbrow Johannesburg, and are generally not South Africans.


Mike: In the mean time while this scam is running they doing another scam, if they can get money out of you that’s what they gonna do

Pedro: I didn’t feel comfortable going to the police at all, and then, more people know what happened.

Mike: The police will not do anything because they don’t have the infrastructure to deal with this kind of crime. There is no guarantee for the privacy of this kind of investigation.

VO: Mike asks the victims to supply him with all the communication and the whatsapp numbers and from that he identifies the syndicates

Mike: We have built a database of all these numbers but the moment they under scrutiny they discard of the numbers

Devi: Once you cut off communication are their threats real, do they ever release those pictures anyway

Mike: They can’t because we have a way we manipulate the information they have’

VO: Jonathan hadn’t been contacted for a few days after Mike’s intervention, but he was still edgy.
Devi: There’s still no relief for you

Jonathan: exactly you don’t know if it’s over yet, or if they just taking a break.

Mike: Sometimes they come back with a different number and we start again.

LINK: So If you feel the urge to share an intimate part of you with a stranger online, it could be the worst snap decision you've ever made.

Social media and text messages are often the source of the sexual material and the threatened means, used to share it with others.
metadata.Summary: In South Africa incidents of Sextortion have been on the rise from 2016 and to date, more and more individuals are falling for it. It used to be that the primary targets and victims for such online attacks are young vulnerable females, but this has since escalated to older victims being blackmailed for cash. With online dating sites such as Tinder, Zoosk and Grinder more adults are targets of the scams. Unscrupulous individuals are lurking on the Internet ready to pounce on unsuspecting victims. Your computer webcam, cellphone and online chats can be hacked by an unknown stranger who will be able to access all intimate information about you. The unknown individual will then invite you to a social media platform, be it Watsapp, Facebook, etc. They would then proceed to blackmail you for money or to perform sexually explicit activities such as sending nude pictures, videos or such. They will then threaten you with publicizing your intimate information on the Internet or alerting your loved ones, church congregations and colleagues of all the information they have.
metadata.Further information: Mike Bolhuis a private investigator has recently had quite a few clients who have approached him to catch the perpetrators or catfish, as they are extorting his clients for a lot of money, to such an extent that they say to their victim, if you don't deposit the money within the next 20 minutes we will publish your information. They then harass the person to take pictures of themselves whilst they are depositing the money and to tell them what they are doing every step of the way. They are also embarrassed and feel they have no recourse, which is why they are approaching a private investigator. According to Dudu Nhlabathi, a Psychologist, traditionally females have been victims that fall for this scam, but now males are equally vulnerable. Males tend to be under the illusion that women are not capable of doing such things, and they feel physically superior, so they tend not to feel the danger. The scamsters study psychological methods when identifying their targets as well. With women It is normally low self-esteem individuals who would be identified for instance those who never post full body pictures on the social media platforms are easily spotted. When it comes to male victims, if they are flashy they can be a target, or if they hold jobs that would be compromised if they are exposed, especially if they are family men they will become instantly vulnerable to sextortion. The scammers appear to be their friends at first to earn their trust and then they pounce once the victims fall for them, or they purely engage with the male victims for a bit of online sexual fun and games. Dr Nhlabathi deals both with Victims and perpetrators. Carte Blanche will possibly also speak to one of the scammers. It is quite clear that the online space is increasingly and quickly becoming a space where people are vulnerable to being blackmailed for their private vices or supposed fun. The search for reassurance and belonging is driving unsuspecting victims to a world of horror and pain. Is there a way to stop these perpetrators and can the victims get retribution? Carte Blanche investigates.
